value: not later than the sixth day after discharge
summary: Texas: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due not later than the sixth day after discharge.
evidence_quote: Sec. 61.014. (a) An employer shall pay in full an employee who is discharged from employment not later than the sixth day after the date the employee is discharged.
source_title: Texas Labor Code, Chapter 61 (Payment of Wages)
notes: Sec. 61.001 defines 'Day' as a calendar day.

value: not later than the next regularly scheduled payday
summary: Texas: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due not later than the next regularly scheduled payday.
evidence_quote: Sec. 61.014. (b) An employer shall pay in full an employee who leaves employment other than by discharge not later than the next regularly scheduled payday.
source_title: Texas Labor Code, Chapter 61 (Payment of Wages)

value: immediately at the time of termination (including accrued vacation)
summary: California: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due immediately at the time of termination (including accrued vacation).
evidence_quote: An employee who is discharged must be paid all of his or her wages, including accrued vacation, immediately at the time of termination. Labor Code Sections 201 and 227.3
source_title: Paydays, pay periods, and the final wages (California DIR, Labor Commissioner's Office)
source_publisher: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Labor Standards Enforcement
notes: Industry exceptions exist (seasonal food processing, motion pictures, oil drilling, venue hiring halls) per the same page.

value: at the time of quitting if 72 hours notice was given; otherwise within 72 hours of quitting
summary: California: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due at the time of quitting if 72 hours notice was given; otherwise within 72 hours of quitting.
evidence_quote: An employee without a written employment contract for a definite period of time who quits without giving 72 hours prior notice must be paid all of his or her wages, including accrued vacation, within 72 hours of quitting. Labor Code Section 202
source_title: Paydays, pay periods, and the final wages (California DIR, Labor Commissioner's Office)
source_publisher: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Labor Standards Enforcement
notes: With at least 72 hours prior notice, wages are due at the time of quitting (Labor Code 202, same page).

value: on or before the next regular payday
summary: North Carolina: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due on or before the next regular payday.
evidence_quote: Employees whose employment is discontinued for any reason shall be paid all wages due on or before the next regular payday either through the regular pay channels or by trackable mail if requested by the employee in writing.
source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 95-25.7, Payment to separated employees

value: on or before the next regular payday
summary: North Carolina: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due on or before the next regular payday.
evidence_quote: Employees whose employment is discontinued for any reason shall be paid all wages due on or before the next regular payday either through the regular pay channels or by trackable mail if requested by the employee in writing.
source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 95-25.7, Payment to separated employees

value: on or before the date the wages would have been paid had employment continued
summary: Virginia: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due on or before the date the wages would have been paid had employment continued.
evidence_quote: Upon termination of employment an employee shall be paid all wages due him for work performed prior thereto; such payment shall be made on or before the date on which he would have been paid for such work had his employment not been terminated.
source_title: Code of Virginia 40.1-29, Time and medium of payment

value: on or before the date the wages would have been paid had employment continued
summary: Virginia: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due on or before the date the wages would have been paid had employment continued.
evidence_quote: Upon termination of employment an employee shall be paid all wages due him for work performed prior thereto; such payment shall be made on or before the date on which he would have been paid for such work had his employment not been terminated.
source_title: Code of Virginia 40.1-29, Time and medium of payment
notes: Statute says 'termination of employment' without distinguishing quit from discharge.

value: not later than the working day following discharge
summary: District of Columbia: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due not later than the working day following discharge.
evidence_quote: (1) Whenever an employer discharges an employee, the employer shall pay the employee's wages earned not later than the working day following such discharge
source_title: D.C. Code 32-1303, Payment of wages upon discharge or resignation
source_publisher: Council of the District of Columbia (D.C. Law Library)
notes: 4-day allowance where the employee is responsible for employer monies (same subsection).

value: next regular payday or within 7 days of quitting, whichever is earlier
summary: District of Columbia: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due next regular payday or within 7 days of quitting, whichever is earlier.
evidence_quote: (2) Whenever an employee (not having a written contract of employment for a period in excess of 30 days) quits or resigns, the employer shall pay the employee's wages due upon the next regular payday or within 7 days from the date of quitting or resigning, whichever is earlier.
source_title: D.C. Code 32-1303, Payment of wages upon discharge or resignation
source_publisher: Council of the District of Columbia (D.C. Law Library)

value: within 24 hours of separation
summary: Utah: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due within 24 hours of separation.
evidence_quote: (1)(a) When an employer separates an employee from the employer's payroll the unpaid wages of the employee become due immediately, and the employer shall pay the wages to the employee within 24 hours of the time of separation at the specified place of payment.
source_title: Utah Code 34-28-5, Separation from payroll, resignation

value: on the next regular payday
summary: Utah: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due on the next regular payday.
evidence_quote: (2) If an employee does not have a written contract for a definite period and resigns the employee's employment, the wages earned and unpaid ... become due and payable on the next regular payday.
source_title: Utah Code 34-28-5, Separation from payroll, resignation

value: on or before the day the wages would have been paid had employment continued
summary: Maryland: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due on or before the day the wages would have been paid had employment continued.
evidence_quote: each employer shall pay an employee or the authorized representative of an employee all wages due for work that the employee performed before the termination of employment, on or before the day on which the employee would have been paid the wages if the employment had not been terminated.

value: on or before the day the wages would have been paid had employment continued
summary: Maryland: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due on or before the day the wages would have been paid had employment continued.
evidence_quote: each employer shall pay an employee or the authorized representative of an employee all wages due for work that the employee performed before the termination of employment, on or before the day on which the employee would have been paid the wages if the employment had not been terminated.

value: not later than the next regular payday
summary: Iowa: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due not later than the next regular payday.
evidence_quote: When the employment of an employee is suspended or terminated, the employer shall pay all wages earned ... not later than the next regular payday for the pay period in which the wages were earned
source_title: Iowa Code 91A.4 (2026), Employment suspension or termination
notes: Commission true-ups due within 30 days (same section).

value: not later than the next regular payday
summary: Iowa: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due not later than the next regular payday.
evidence_quote: When the employment of an employee is suspended or terminated, the employer shall pay all wages earned ... not later than the next regular payday for the pay period in which the wages were earned
source_title: Iowa Code 91A.4 (2026), Employment suspension or termination

value: immediately, as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined
summary: Michigan: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due immediately, as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined.
evidence_quote: (2) An employer shall immediately pay to an employee who has been discharged from employment all wages earned and due, as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined.

value: as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined
summary: Michigan: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined.
evidence_quote: (1) An employer shall pay to an employee voluntarily leaving employment all wages earned and due, as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined.

value: at the end of the established pay period
summary: Washington: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due at the end of the established pay period.
evidence_quote: (2) When any employee shall cease to work for an employer, whether by discharge or by voluntary withdrawal, the wages due him or her on account of his or her employment shall be paid to him or her at the end of the established pay period
source_title: RCW 49.48.010, Payment of wages due to employee ceasing work

value: at the end of the established pay period
summary: Washington: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due at the end of the established pay period.
evidence_quote: (2) When any employee shall cease to work for an employer, whether by discharge or by voluntary withdrawal, the wages due him or her on account of his or her employment shall be paid to him or her at the end of the established pay period
source_title: RCW 49.48.010, Payment of wages due to employee ceasing work

value: no later than the employer's usual regularly scheduled payroll date
summary: Wyoming: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due no later than the employer's usual regularly scheduled payroll date.
evidence_quote: (a) Whenever an employee quits service or is discharged, the employee shall be paid whatever wages are due him ... no later than the employer's usual practice on regularly scheduled payroll dates or at a time specified under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement

value: no later than the employer's usual regularly scheduled payroll date
summary: Wyoming: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due no later than the employer's usual regularly scheduled payroll date.
evidence_quote: (a) Whenever an employee quits service or is discharged, the employee shall be paid whatever wages are due him ... no later than the employer's usual practice on regularly scheduled payroll dates or at a time specified under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement

value: at separation if possible, and no later than the next regularly scheduled payday
summary: Illinois: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due at separation if possible, and no later than the next regularly scheduled payday.
evidence_quote: Every employer shall pay the final compensation of separated employees in full, at the time of separation, if possible, but in no case later than the next regularly scheduled payday for such employee.
source_title: 820 ILCS 115/5, Illinois Wage Payment and Collection Act
notes: Earned vacation must be paid out as part of final compensation (same section).

value: at separation if possible, and no later than the next regularly scheduled payday
summary: Illinois: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due at separation if possible, and no later than the next regularly scheduled payday.
evidence_quote: Every employer shall pay the final compensation of separated employees in full, at the time of separation, if possible, but in no case later than the next regularly scheduled payday for such employee.
source_title: 820 ILCS 115/5, Illinois Wage Payment and Collection Act

value: not later than the next regular payday
summary: Pennsylvania: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due not later than the next regular payday.
evidence_quote: (a) Separated Employes. Whenever an employer separates an employe from the payroll, or whenever an employe quits or resigns his employment, the wages or compensation earned shall become due and payable not later than the next regular payday of his employer on which such wages would otherwise be due and payable.
source_title: Wage Payment and Collection Law, Act of 1961 P.L. 637 No. 329, Section 5 (PA DLI copy)
source_publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry

value: not later than the next regular payday
summary: Pennsylvania: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due not later than the next regular payday.
evidence_quote: (a) Separated Employes. Whenever an employer separates an employe from the payroll, or whenever an employe quits or resigns his employment, the wages or compensation earned shall become due and payable not later than the next regular payday of his employer on which such wages would otherwise be due and payable.
source_title: Wage Payment and Collection Law, Act of 1961 P.L. 637 No. 329, Section 5 (PA DLI copy)
source_publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry

value: at the regular payday for the pay period in which separation occurred
summary: Indiana: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due at the regular payday for the pay period in which separation occurred.
evidence_quote: Sec. 2. (a) Whenever any employer separates any employee from the pay-roll, the unpaid wages or compensation of such employee shall become due and payable at regular pay day for pay period in which separation occurred

value: not required until the next usual and regular payday
summary: Indiana: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due not required until the next usual and regular payday.
evidence_quote: if an employee voluntarily leaves employment, either permanently or temporarily, the employer shall not be required to pay the employee an amount due the employee until the next usual and regular day for payment of wages, as established by the employer.

value: next regular payday or within 15 days of discharge, whichever occurs first
summary: Louisiana: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due next regular payday or within 15 days of discharge, whichever occurs first.
evidence_quote: A.(1)(a) Upon the discharge of any laborer or other employee ... on or before the next regular payday or no later than fifteen days following the date of discharge, whichever occurs first.
source_title: Louisiana R.S. 23:631, Discharge or resignation of employees

value: next regular payday for that pay cycle or within 15 days of resignation, whichever occurs first
summary: Louisiana: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due next regular payday for that pay cycle or within 15 days of resignation, whichever occurs first.
evidence_quote: (b) Upon the resignation of any laborer or other employee ... on or before the next regular payday for the pay cycle during which the employee was working at the time of separation or no later than fifteen days following the date of resignation, whichever occurs first.
source_title: Louisiana R.S. 23:631, Discharge or resignation of employees

value: next regular payday or 21 days after discharge, whichever occurs last
summary: Tennessee: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due next regular payday or 21 days after discharge, whichever occurs last.
evidence_quote: Any employee who leaves or is discharged from employment shall be paid in full all wages or salary earned by the employee no later than the next regular pay day following the date of dismissal or voluntary leaving, or twenty-one (21) days following the date of discharge or voluntary leaving, whichever occurs last. There is no exemption under the law. Tenn. Code. Ann. 50-2-103 (g)
source_title: Wages & Breaks (Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development)
source_publisher: Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development
notes: Tennessee payday rules apply to private employers with 5 or more employees (same page).

value: next regular payday or 21 days after leaving, whichever occurs last
summary: Tennessee: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due next regular payday or 21 days after leaving, whichever occurs last.
evidence_quote: Any employee who leaves or is discharged from employment shall be paid in full all wages or salary earned by the employee no later than the next regular pay day following the date of dismissal or voluntary leaving, or twenty-one (21) days following the date of discharge or voluntary leaving, whichever occurs last. There is no exemption under the law. Tenn. Code. Ann. 50-2-103 (g)
source_title: Wages & Breaks (Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development)
source_publisher: Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development

value: no later than the next regular payday for that pay
summary: New York: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due no later than the next regular payday for that pay.
evidence_quote: Employees whose employment has ended are entitled to be paid no later than the pay day on which their next pay would have been due had they still been employed. Upon request of the employee, employers are required to mail the employee his or her wages.
source_title: Frequency of Pay Frequently Asked Questions (NYS DOL)
source_publisher: New York State Department of Labor
notes: NY Labor Law Section 191. FAQ covers termination, retirement, or resignation.

value: no later than the next regular payday for that pay
summary: New York: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due no later than the next regular payday for that pay.
evidence_quote: Employees whose employment has ended are entitled to be paid no later than the pay day on which their next pay would have been due had they still been employed. Upon request of the employee, employers are required to mail the employee his or her wages.
source_title: Frequency of Pay Frequently Asked Questions (NYS DOL)
source_publisher: New York State Department of Labor

value: within 7 working days or by the end of the next regular pay period, whichever is sooner
summary: Arizona: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due within 7 working days or by the end of the next regular pay period, whichever is sooner.
evidence_quote: A. When an employee is discharged from the service of an employer, he shall be paid wages due him within seven working days or the end of the next regular pay period, whichever is sooner.

value: no later than the regular payday for the pay period in which termination occurred
summary: Arizona: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due no later than the regular payday for the pay period in which termination occurred.
evidence_quote: B. When an employee quits the service of an employer he shall be paid in the usual manner all wages due him no later than the regular payday for the pay period during which the termination occurred

value: in full on the day of discharge
summary: Massachusetts: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due in full on the day of discharge.
evidence_quote: any employee discharged from such employment shall be paid in full on the day of his discharge

value: in full on the following regular payday
summary: Massachusetts: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due in full on the following regular payday.
evidence_quote: any employee leaving his employment shall be paid in full on the following regular pay day, and, in the absence of a regular pay day, on the following Saturday

value: within 48 hours of separation or by the next regular payday (not more than 30 days)
summary: South Carolina: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due within 48 hours of separation or by the next regular payday (not more than 30 days).
evidence_quote: When an employer separates an employee from the payroll for any reason, the employer shall pay all wages due to the employee within forty-eight hours of the time of separation or the next regular payday which may not exceed thirty days.

value: within 48 hours of separation or by the next regular payday (not more than 30 days)
summary: South Carolina: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due within 48 hours of separation or by the next regular payday (not more than 30 days).
evidence_quote: When an employer separates an employee from the payroll for any reason, the employer shall pay all wages due to the employee within forty-eight hours of the time of separation or the next regular payday which may not exceed thirty days.
notes: Statute applies when the employer 'separates an employee from the payroll for any reason'; confirm how SC applies it to voluntary quits.

value: due on the day of discharge (employee may request payment in writing)
summary: Missouri: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due due on the day of discharge (employee may request payment in writing).
evidence_quote: Whenever any person, firm or corporation doing business in this state shall discharge, with or without cause, or refuse to further employ any servant or employee thereof, the unpaid wages of the servant or employee then earned at the contract rate, without abatement or deduction, shall be and become due and payable on the day of the discharge
source_publisher: Revisor of Statutes, State of Missouri
notes: Penalty provisions apply after the employee's written request (same section).
290.110 covers discharge only; no resignation rule confirmed from an official source this session.

value: immediately upon the employee's demand; default if not paid within 24 hours after demand
summary: Minnesota: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due immediately upon the employee's demand; default if not paid within 24 hours after demand.
evidence_quote: (a) When any employer employing labor within this state discharges an employee, the wages or commissions actually earned and unpaid at the time of the discharge are immediately due and payable upon demand of the employee. ... If the employee's earned wages and commissions are not paid within 24 hours after demand ... the employer is in default.
source_publisher: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes

value: not later than the first regularly scheduled payday after the final day of employment
summary: Minnesota: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due not later than the first regularly scheduled payday after the final day of employment.
evidence_quote: (a) When any such employee quits or resigns employment, the wages or commissions earned and unpaid at the time the employee quits or resigns shall be paid in full not later than the first regularly scheduled payday following the employee's final day of employment
source_publisher: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
notes: Further timing rules apply in some cases (see 181.14).

value: next regular payday or within two weeks of termination, whichever is sooner
summary: Nebraska: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due next regular payday or within two weeks of termination, whichever is sooner.
evidence_quote: (a) Whenever an employer, other than a political subdivision, separates an employee from the payroll, the unpaid wages shall become due on the next regular payday or within two weeks of the date of termination, whichever is sooner

value: next regular payday or within two weeks of termination, whichever is sooner
summary: Nebraska: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due next regular payday or within two weeks of termination, whichever is sooner.
evidence_quote: (a) Whenever an employer, other than a political subdivision, separates an employee from the payroll, the unpaid wages shall become due on the next regular payday or within two weeks of the date of termination, whichever is sooner
notes: Statute uses 'separates an employee from the payroll'; confirm application to voluntary quits.

value: not later than the next regular payday
summary: Kansas: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due not later than the next regular payday.
evidence_quote: (a) Whenever an employer discharges an employee or whenever an employee quits or resigns, the employer shall pay the employee's earned wages not later than the next regular payday upon which he or she would have been paid if still employed
source_publisher: Kansas Office of Revisor of Statutes

value: not later than the next regular payday
summary: Kansas: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due not later than the next regular payday.
evidence_quote: (a) Whenever an employer discharges an employee or whenever an employee quits or resigns, the employer shall pay the employee's earned wages not later than the next regular payday upon which he or she would have been paid if still employed
source_publisher: Kansas Office of Revisor of Statutes

value: in full within 72 hours of discharge
summary: New Hampshire: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due in full within 72 hours of discharge.
evidence_quote: I. Whenever an employer discharges an employee, the employer shall pay the employee's wages in full within 72 hours.

value: no later than the next regular payday (within 72 hours if one pay period's notice was given)
summary: New Hampshire: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due no later than the next regular payday (within 72 hours if one pay period's notice was given).
evidence_quote: II. Whenever an employee quits or resigns, the employer shall pay the employee's wages no later than the next regular payday ... except that if the employee gives at least one pay period's notice of intention to quit the employer shall pay all wages earned by the employee within 72 hours.

value: no later than the next established payday
summary: Maine: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due no later than the next established payday.
evidence_quote: An employee leaving employment must be paid in full no later than the employee's next established payday.

value: no later than the next established payday
summary: Maine: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due no later than the next established payday.
evidence_quote: An employee leaving employment must be paid in full no later than the employee's next established payday.

value: on the next regular payday
summary: Rhode Island: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due on the next regular payday.
evidence_quote: (a) Whenever an employee separates or is separated from the payroll of an employer, the unpaid wages or compensation of the employee shall become due on the next regular payday and payable at the usual place of payment.
notes: Accrued vacation after one year of service is payable with final wages (same section).

value: on the next regular payday
summary: Rhode Island: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due on the next regular payday.
evidence_quote: (a) Whenever an employee separates or is separated from the payroll of an employer, the unpaid wages or compensation of the employee shall become due on the next regular payday and payable at the usual place of payment.

value: immediately upon separation for cause or layoff, unless a written policy extends it to the next regular payday or 15 days, whichever first
summary: Montana: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due immediately upon separation for cause or layoff, unless a written policy extends it to the next regular payday or 15 days, whichever first.
evidence_quote: (2) Except as provided in subsection (3), when an employee is separated for cause or laid off from employment by the employer, all the unpaid wages of the employee are due and payable immediately upon separation unless the employer has a written personnel policy governing the employment that extends the time for payment of final wages to the employee's next regular payday for the pay period or to within 15 days from the separation, whichever occurs first.

value: next regular payday for that pay period or 15 days from separation, whichever occurs first
summary: Montana: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due next regular payday for that pay period or 15 days from separation, whichever occurs first.
evidence_quote: (1) Except as provided in subsection (2) or (3), when an employee separates from the employ of any employer, all the unpaid wages of the employee are due and payable on the next regular payday for the pay period during which the employee was separated from employment or 15 days from the date of separation from employment, whichever occurs first

value: earlier of the next regular payday or 10 days (weekends and holidays excluded)
summary: Idaho: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due earlier of the next regular payday or 10 days (weekends and holidays excluded).
evidence_quote: (1) Upon layoff, or upon termination of employment by either the employer or employee, the employer shall pay or make available at the usual place of payment all wages then due the employee by the earlier of the next regularly scheduled payday or within ten (10) days of such layoff or termination, weekends and holidays excluded.
notes: If the employee makes a written request, wages are due within 48 hours of the request, weekends and holidays excluded (same section).

value: earlier of the next regular payday or 10 days (weekends and holidays excluded)
summary: Idaho: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due earlier of the next regular payday or 10 days (weekends and holidays excluded).
evidence_quote: (1) Upon layoff, or upon termination of employment by either the employer or employee, the employer shall pay or make available at the usual place of payment all wages then due the employee by the earlier of the next regularly scheduled payday or within ten (10) days of such layoff or termination, weekends and holidays excluded.

value: within 72 hours of discharge
summary: Vermont: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due within 72 hours of discharge.
evidence_quote: (b) An employee who: ... (2) is discharged from employment shall be paid within 72 hours of discharge

value: on the last regular payday (or the following Friday if there is no regular payday)
summary: Vermont: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due on the last regular payday (or the following Friday if there is no regular payday).
evidence_quote: (b) An employee who: (1) voluntarily leaves employment shall be paid on the last regular pay day, or if there is no regular pay day, on the following Friday

value: later of the next regular pay date or 3 business days after the last day worked
summary: Delaware: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due later of the next regular pay date or 3 business days after the last day worked.
evidence_quote: (a) (1) Whenever an employee quits, resigns, is discharged, suspended, or laid off, the wages earned by the employee become due and payable by the employer on the later of the following: a. The next date the wages would be paid through the last day worked under the employer's regular pay cycle as if the employment had not stopped. b. Three business days after the last day worked.

value: later of the next regular pay date or 3 business days after the last day worked
summary: Delaware: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due later of the next regular pay date or 3 business days after the last day worked.
evidence_quote: (a) (1) Whenever an employee quits, resigns, is discharged, suspended, or laid off, the wages earned by the employee become due and payable by the employer on the later of the following: a. The next date the wages would be paid through the last day worked under the employer's regular pay cycle as if the employment had not stopped. b. Three business days after the last day worked.

value: not later than the next regular payday (or once employer property is returned, if later)
summary: South Dakota: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due not later than the next regular payday (or once employer property is returned, if later).
evidence_quote: Whenever an employer separates an employee from the payroll, the unpaid wages or compensation of such employee are due and payable not later than the next regular stated pay day for which those hours would have normally been paid or as soon thereafter as the employee returns to the employer all property of the employer in the employee's possession.

notes: 60-11-10 covers separation by the employer; the resignation rule (60-11-11) was not fetched this session.

value: immediately upon discharge
summary: Nevada: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due immediately upon discharge.
evidence_quote: 1. Whenever an employer discharges an employee, the wages and compensation earned and unpaid at the time of such discharge shall become due and payable immediately.

value: the earlier of the regular payday or 7 days after quitting

evidence_quote: Whenever an employee resigns or quits his or her employment, the wages and compensation earned and unpaid at the time of the employees resignation or quitting must be paid no later than: 1. value: not later than the end of the first business day after discharge
summary: Oregon: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due not later than the end of the first business day after discharge.
evidence_quote: (1) When an employer discharges an employee or when employment is terminated by mutual agreement, all wages earned and unpaid at the time of the discharge or termination become due and payable not later than the end of the first business day after the discharge or termination.

value: immediately with 48 hours notice; otherwise within 5 days (excluding weekends and holidays) or the next regular payday, whichever is first
summary: Oregon: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due immediately with 48 hours notice; otherwise within 5 days (excluding weekends and holidays) or the next regular payday, whichever is first.
evidence_quote: (2)(a) ... all wages earned and unpaid at the time of quitting become due and payable immediately if the employee has given to the employer not less than 48 hours notice ... (b) ... the wages become due and payable within five days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and holidays, after the employee has quit, or at the next regularly scheduled payday after the employee has quit, whichever event first occurs.
notes: Special estimate rule applies when the employee submits time records (652.140(2)(c)).

value: by the next regular payday (or the 31-day deadline in 109.03(1), if earlier)
summary: Wisconsin: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due by the next regular payday (or the 31-day deadline in 109.03(1), if earlier).
evidence_quote: Any employee, except a sales agent employed on a commission basis, not having a written contract for a definite period, who quits employment or who is discharged from employment shall be paid in full by no later than the date on which the employee regularly would have been paid under the employer's established payroll schedule or the date of payment required under sub. (1), whichever is earlier.

value: immediately (with short extensions if the payroll unit is not operating)
summary: Colorado: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due immediately (with short extensions if the payroll unit is not operating).
evidence_quote: (1) (a) When an interruption in the employer-employee relationship by volition of the employer occurs, the wages or compensation for labor or service earned, vested, determinable, and unpaid at the time of such discharge is due and payable immediately.
source_title: Colorado Wage Act (C.R.S. 8-4-109), CDLE compilation revised August 12, 2026
source_publisher: Colorado Department of Labor and Employment
notes: If the accounting unit is not operating: within 6 hours of its next regular workday, or 24 hours if off site (same subsection).

value: upon the next regular payday
summary: Colorado: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due upon the next regular payday.
evidence_quote: (b) When an employee quits or resigns such employee's employment, the wages or compensation shall become due and payable upon the next regular payday.
source_title: Colorado Wage Act (C.R.S. 8-4-109), CDLE compilation revised August 12, 2026
source_publisher: Colorado Department of Labor and Employment

value: not later than the regular payday for the pay period in which employment ended
summary: New Jersey: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due not later than the regular payday for the pay period in which employment ended.
evidence_quote: Whenever an employer discharges an employee, ... or whenever an employee quits, resigns, or leaves employment for any reason, the employer shall pay the employee all wages due not later than the regular payday for the pay period during which the employee's termination, suspension or cessation of employment (whether temporary or permanent) took place
source_title: Selected NJ State Labor Laws and Regulations (N.J.S.A. 34:11-4.3)
source_publisher: New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development

value: no later than the next business day after discharge
summary: Connecticut: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due no later than the next business day after discharge.
evidence_quote: (b) Whenever an employer discharges an Employee, the employer shall pay the employee's wages in full no later than the business day next succeeding the date of such discharge.
source_title: Connecticut Wage Payment Laws (CT DOL compilation, Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-71c)
notes: Laid-off employees: not later than the next regular payday (31-71c(c)).

value: not later than the next regular payday
summary: Connecticut: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due not later than the next regular payday.
evidence_quote: (a) Whenever an employee voluntarily terminates his employment, the employer shall pay the employee's wages in full not later than the next regular pay day
source_title: Connecticut Wage Payment Laws (CT DOL compilation, Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-71c)

value: next normal pay period or 14 days after dismissal, whichever occurs last
summary: Kentucky: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due next normal pay period or 14 days after dismissal, whichever occurs last.
evidence_quote: Any employee who leaves or is discharged from his employment shall be paid in full all wages or salary earned by him; not later than the next normal pay period following the date of dismissal or voluntary leaving or fourteen (14) days following such date of dismissal or voluntary leaving whichever last occurs.

value: next normal pay period or 14 days after leaving, whichever occurs last
summary: Kentucky: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due next normal pay period or 14 days after leaving, whichever occurs last.
evidence_quote: Any employee who leaves or is discharged from his employment shall be paid in full all wages or salary earned by him; not later than the next normal pay period following the date of dismissal or voluntary leaving or fourteen (14) days following such date of dismissal or voluntary leaving whichever last occurs.
